about.title: Fountain Valley Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast — a wet floor at a shopping center off Euclid, a cracked walkway near an apartment complex, poor lighting in a parking structure along Edinger. In Fountain Valley, a city of nearly 57,000 residents wedged between Brookhurst and the 405, property owners still carry a legal duty to keep their spaces reasonably safe. When they don't, and someone gets hurt, California law allows an injured person to pursue compensation, though proving the owner knew or should have known about the hazard is often the hardest part of the case. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free connection service that matches you with an independent attorney who understands how these claims work locally. If a fall left you with medical bills, missed work, or lingering pain, it's worth having someone look at what happened before evidence disappears or memories fade.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Premises Law

items.title: Notice Is the Central Question
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather the facts needed to establish that notice.

items.title: Video and Physical Evidence Fades Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage at Fountain Valley businesses is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of video can make a meaningful difference in a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though your share of fault may reduce the amount recovered.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Fountain Valley?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or park, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier formal claim. Because these timelines vary, it helps to have a claim reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell at a store near Brookhurst or Euclid and didn't report it right away?
items.answer: Not reporting immediately doesn't automatically bar a claim, but it can make proving what happened more difficult. Try to document the scene with photos, note witnesses, and request that the business preserve any surveillance footage as soon as possible. An attorney can help you gather this evidence even after the fact.

items.question: Do I need to prove the property owner was negligent on purpose?
items.answer: No, California premises liability law doesn't require intent. You generally need to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and failed to address it within a reasonable time. This is often the most contested part of a slip and fall case, which is why documentation matters so much.
